New Delhi: At the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, approval has been given to the City Investments to Innovate, Integrate and Sustain 2.0 scheme, called CITIIS 2.0. CITIIS 2.0 is a scheme developed by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs in partnership with the French Development Agency (AFD), the Credit Institution for Reconstruction (KfW), the European Union (EU) and the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA). This scheme will be implemented for four years, that is, from 2023 to 2027. The scheme will support competitive projects that promote the circular economy by focusing on integrated waste management at the city level, climate-oriented reform actions at the state level, and institutional strengthening and knowledge dissemination at the national level. The funding for CITIIS 2.0 includes a loan of Rs.1,760 crore (200 million euros - AFD and KfW 100 million euros each) and a technical assistance grant of Rs.106 crore (12 million euros) provided by the European Union. CITIIS 2.0 aims to build on and scale up the experience and successes of CITIIS 1.0. It is noteworthy that the total cost of CITIIS 1.0 was Rs. 933 crore (106 million euros).

headline_en: Remember Jung Da-bin of “Rooftop Room Cat” and “He Was Cool”? 19 years have passed since she “lost her life in her boyfriend's bathroom”, grieving mother held a ghost marriage
text_en:
Remember Jung Da-bin of “Rooftop Room Cat” and “He Was Cool”? 19 years have passed since she “lost her life in her boyfriend's bathroom”, grieving mother held a ghost marriage

Time flies. For the Korean actress Jung Da-bin, who won people's hearts with her sweet smile, 10 February marks the 19th anniversary of her death. On 10 February 2007, she was found dead at just 27 years old in the bathroom of her boyfriend's residence in Gangnam District, Seoul. No suicide note was left at the scene, and although the police performed an autopsy, they could not find evidence of homicide, and the case was finally closed as a suicide.
Her sudden death shocked all of Korea. Jung Da-bin debuted in 2000 playing the teenage version of Choi Jin-sil's character in the film “Sad Love Song”, then became popular with her lively and cute image in the MBC sitcom “Nonstop”, went on to become the queen of romantic comedy with “Rooftop Room Cat” (Attic Man and Woman), and then showed her sunny charm in works such as “Sister-in-law Is Nineteen” and “He Was Cool”, being hailed as the “romantic comedy fairy”.
However, behind the glow lay hidden pain unknown to others. In the early hours of the day before her death, she left a post titled “After All” on her personal mini-homepage, writing: “I feel suffocated and want to die. I get angry for no reason, I'm going crazy. It feels as bad as seasickness. I feel like I've lost myself, I'm losing some sense of identity.” These words left fans deeply heartbroken.
Since she had already been confirmed to appear in the new dramas “Cube” and “Rally” before her death, her family and agency questioned the cause of death, believing she had no reason to commit suicide, and requested a reinvestigation, but in the end the verdict could not be overturned. Jung Da-bin's death left many doubts, and all kinds of speculation have never ceased over the years.
After her death, the way her mother expressed her longing was also heartbreaking. A programme once aired footage of her mother attempting to “communicate with spirits”, and in 2011, on the 4th anniversary of her daughter's death, a “ghost marriage ceremony” was held for her according to her mother's wishes. These acts all reflect the indelible pain of her closest family.
19 years have passed, and Jung Da-bin's signature radiant smile still remains in the hearts of many fans to this day. Whenever Korean stars who died young are mentioned, her name is always brought up with regret and memories.

headline_en: Inheritance in Ukraine — what share children are guaranteed to receive
text_en: Inheritance in Ukraine — what share children are guaranteed to receive Every person can decide in advance the fate of their property after death by drawing up a will. In it, any heirs can be named — both relatives and outsiders, enterprises, organisations or even the state. The Ministry of Justice of Ukraine explained whether minor children can receive an inheritance and what is needed for this. Can children be deprived of inheritance The testator also has the right to disinherit any of the legal heirs. At the same time, the law guarantees a compulsory share of the inheritance for certain categories of persons. These are: young, minor and adult disabled children of the deceased; children conceived during the testator's lifetime but born after his death. They are entitled to half of the share that would belong to them by law. How to accept an inheritance In general, for this it is necessary to submit an application to a notary within six months from the day of the testator's death. However, there are exceptions: if the heir lived together with the deceased, he is automatically considered to have accepted the inheritance, unless he has renounced it; children are also considered to have accepted the inheritance, even without an application, if they have not officially renounced their rights. The application on behalf of children is submitted by parents or guardians, but from the age of 14 teenagers can apply to a notary on their own. Inheritance is not only property, but also debts. headline_en: Military personnel may be exempted from criminal liability for a first desertion
text_en: Military personnel may be exempted from criminal liability for a first desertion The Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine adopted as a basis a bill that exempts military personnel from criminal liability for a first unauthorised leaving of a military unit or desertion, if they voluntarily return to service and receive written consent from the commander, reports Dzerkalo Tyzhnia. As MP Yaroslav Zhelezniak noted, bill No. 11322 was supported in the first reading by 273 MPs. According to the proposed changes to legislation, the offender must return to the unit or to the place of service before the end of the proceedings, and the commander must give consent for such a person to continue military service. Such consent must be drawn up in writing and handed over to the prosecutor. text_en: In Italy a mako shark has been sighted not far from the coast It is one of the fastest predators in the oceans and it has been sighted a short distance from the Italian coast. A mako shark was the protagonist of a special encounter in Salento, to be precise in Porto Cesareo. It is an event that highlights the richness and fragility of the biodiversity of our seas, which should push us towards a greater knowledge of these creatures and of the challenges to their survival. A mako shark off Porto Cesareo The encounter took place on the evening of Sunday 10 August, five miles from the coast of Porto Cesareo, in Salento. During a tuna fishing trip, Francesco Baldieri and his father Paolo came across a young mako shark, about one metre long. “A beautiful shark, a stupendous creature – explains Francesco Baldieri, instructor and environmental guide, to Repubblica – that came right under the dinghy, as if it wanted to play. headline_en: Conflict with employer led to the arrest of VENUS-1 — diplomats intervened
text_en: Conflict with employer led to the arrest of VENUS-1 — diplomats intervened The fishing vessel VENUS-1 with 13 Russian citizens on board has been arrested in Namibia. This was reported by the Russian embassy in the country. According to the diplomatic mission, the cause was a labour dispute between the crew and the owner of the vessel — the private company Hodago fishing. The conflict arose at the beginning of 2026 over two months of unpaid wages. As specified, after the intervention of the International Transport Workers' Federation, the vessel was arrested and is moored at the berth in the port of Walvis Bay together with the crew. Russian diplomats are working with the Namibian authorities to resolve the situation. The embassy maintains contact with the captain and the sailors, and is also organising the supply of fuel and food to the vessel. The diplomatic mission stressed that there is no threat to the life and health of the Russians. The Namibian side, according to the embassy, is not preventing their return home. The crew made the decision to stay and seek a settlement of the conflict on its own. Work to resolve the situation is continuing. The diplomats stated their intention to seek respect for the rights of Russian citizens and a speedy end to the dispute. Read also: Russian sailors are living on an arrested vessel in Africa.

headline_en: Graffiti and protests. A European capital has joined the wave of anti-tourism
text_en: Graffiti and protests. A European capital has joined the wave of anti-tourism The capital of Greece has joined the wave of protests against excessive tourism that has been spreading across Europe since last year. Now the walls of buildings in Athens are covered with graffiti with anti-tourist inscriptions. Residents are increasingly complaining about the housing crisis, RBC-Ukraine reports, citing greekcitytimes.com. Greece, which is one of the most popular countries in Europe among tourists, is now suffering from excessive tourism. Athens greets guests with graffiti on the walls bearing threatening inscriptions. Last month, residents of the historic city took to the streets to express their dissatisfaction with the influx of tourists. Protesters complain not only about overcrowding due to the large number of tourists, but also about the "displacement" of local residents from their homes. Because of the housing crisis, aggravated by tourism, city dwellers are forced to move. On the buildings one can see inscriptions: "Tourists, go home! The Greek state kills", "Tourism kills the city", "No tourists – no hipsters", "Burn Airbnb". The anti-tourist actions in Athens reflect similar movements across Europe, from Menorca to the Canary Islands, where residents demand measures to reduce the negative consequences of mass tourism. As a reminder, we wrote that a popular European city has declared war on tourists. The centre of Malaga is plastered with stickers with anti-tourism slogans.
